doc: Famous terrestrial analog REGIONS for Moon and Mars (STANDARDS 10.13, 'Discoveries'). Each region is a circle approximation, stated as such. Centre: the coordinate given in the extent source, or the analog source. Radius rules: 'equal_area' = radius of a circle with the same area as the area stated in the extent source (sqrt(A/pi)); 'half_diameter' = half of the diameter stated in the extent source; 'length' = the stated river length, circle centred on the mouth; 'default_conservative_100km' = no extent could be sourced, radius 100 km (lead decision 2026-11-14: when in doubt, mark as known). Inclusion rule (lead decision 2026-11-14, conservative): a region is included if ANY opened source calls it a planetary, Mars or Moon analog (the analog source alone is enough); the extent is taken from a separate opened source when one exists. Regions with no readable analog source (Black Point / SP Crater / Cinder Lake, Colorado Plateau as a whole, Tenerife, Namibia, Ladakh) are not listed. Used by the Earth-context and novelty steps only; never by the score. Opened 2026-11-14.

regions.name: Atacama Desert (Chile)
regions.radius_rule: half_length: length 'nearly 1,600 kilometres' along the coast of northern Chile from near Arica (18 24 S) to near La Serena (29 55 S), Wikipedia 'Atacama Desert' (WWF ecoregion sentence, read by the lead 2026-11-14); radius = half the length = 800 km; centre = midpoint of Arica and La Serena along the coast, lat -24.15, lon -70.2 (lead)
regions.analog_quote: The Atacama is the driest non-polar desert in the world and is a suitable analog for ancient Mars.

regions.name: Mojave Desert and Death Valley (California, USA)
regions.radius_rule: equal_area: area 81,000 km2 (extent source infobox). The article text says 54,000 sq mi; the infobox value is used. FLAG (lead, 2026-11-14): elongated, no length sourced (the search summaries give no reliable NW-SE length); half_length NOT applied
regions.analog_quote: The Mojave Desert/Death Valley region is considered a Mars analog site by the Terrestrial Analogs Panel (LPSC 2011, NASA technical report record).

regions.name: Meteor Crater (Arizona, USA), Colorado Plateau
regions.radius_rule: half_diameter: diameter 1.2 km (NASA page); the crater itself, without ejecta
regions.analog_quote: Graduate students train to study impact craters on Earth, the Moon, Mars, and other planets.

regions.name: Craters of the Moon National Monument and Preserve (Idaho, USA)
regions.radius_rule: equal_area: area 753,000 acres = 3,047 km2 (extent source infobox)
regions.analog_quote: NASA scientists conducting research at Craters of the Moon in preparation for future Mars missions (photo caption).

regions.name: Qaidam Basin (Qinghai, China)
regions.radius_rule: equal_area: area 120,000 km2 (extent source infobox). FLAG (lead, 2026-11-14): the basin is elongated (about 850 km east-west by the WWF ecoregion page, search summary only: that page returned 403); no length was sourced, so half_length NOT applied and the radius is kept
regions.analog_quote: The landscape has some similarity with Mars: almost total lack of vegetation and wind-formed landscape (USGS, 1988).

regions.name: Lanzarote (Canary Islands, Spain)
regions.radius_rule: default_conservative_100km: the island is elongated and no length could be sourced in the article read (only area 845.94 km2); radius 100 km around the island centre covers it
regions.analog_quote: ESA's Pangaea course is devoted to field geology in a 'planetary analogue' with terrain resembling Mars (ESA, 24 Oct 2016).

regions.name: Svalbard (Norway)
regions.radius_rule: equal_area: area 62,045 km2 (extent source infobox). FLAG (lead, 2026-11-14): elongated archipelago, no length sourced; half_length NOT applied
regions.analog_quote: Many geologic phenomena in this cold arctic environment are analogous to landforms on Mars (DLR Europlanet page 'Svalbard - A terrestrial cold-climate analog for Mars').

regions.name: Rio Tinto, river and basin (Huelva, Spain)
regions.radius_rule: length: river length 100 km (extent source infobox); circle centred on the mouth, so the whole river reach lies within it
regions.analog_quote: The Rio Tinto area is an important analog to searching for life in liquid water, deep beneath the subsurface of Mars (Carol Stoker, NASA, 5 Oct 2003).

regions.name: Nordlinger Ries impact crater (Germany)
regions.radius_rule: half_diameter: diameter 24 km (extent source infobox)
regions.analog_quote: Lambert & Reimold (2023), 'Terrestrial impact sites as field analogs for planetary exploration': 'Ries, Rochechouart, and Steinheim score highest, with a small advantage for Ries.'

regions.name: Sudbury Basin (Ontario, Canada)
regions.radius_rule: half_diameter: original diameter 130 km (extent source infobox). The present-day eroded structure is smaller; the original size is used so the whole structure lies within the circle
regions.analog_quote: Lambert & Reimold (2023): 'Sudbury and Meteor Crater score similarly, yet much lower than the leaders' as field analogs for planetary exploration.

regions.name: Haughton impact crater, Devon Island (Nunavut, Canada)
regions.radius_rule: half_diameter: diameter 23 km (extent source infobox)
regions.analog_quote: Using the Haughton Crater as an analog for Mars helps scientists understand the planet's geology and glaciology, as well as field test exploration vehicle technologies (CBC, Haughton-Mars Project).

regions.name: Holuhraun lava flow field (Iceland)
regions.radius_rule: equal_area: lava field of more than 85 km2 (extent source); minimum radius. Iceland as a whole is not used: the analog paper is about Holuhraun
regions.analog_quote: The Holuhraun eruption 'serves as a terrestrial analog for volcanic terrains in Elysium Planitia' (Planetary Science Journal, 2025).

regions.name: El Pinacate y Gran Desierto de Altar Biosphere Reserve (Sonora, Mexico)
regions.radius_rule: equal_area: biosphere reserve area 2,695.05 km2 (extent source infobox); the volcanic field lies within it
regions.analog_quote: Planetary Science Institute (2024): 'Investigations of Lava Flows in the Pinacate Volcanic Field as Analogues for Mars', for a NASA project comparing volcanic features on Earth and Mars.

regions.name: Henry Mountains and Hanksville area (southern Utah, USA)
regions.radius_rule: default_conservative_100km: no extent sourced. Centre: Wikipedia 'Henry Mountains' infobox coordinate 38 06.53 N, 110 48.82 W
regions.analog_quote: 'Just a few kilometers further, the terrain near Hanksville looks almost Mars-like' (visitutah.com article, German original: 'fast wie auf dem Mars'; read 2026-11-14).

regions.name: Mars Desert Research Station (Utah, USA)
regions.radius_rule: default_conservative_100km: no extent sourced; the station is a single habitat site
regions.analog_quote: Mars Desert Research Station: 'A Mars habitat simulation where scientists work' (visitutah.com article, read 2026-11-14).

regions.name: McMurdo Dry Valleys (Antarctica)
regions.radius_rule: default_conservative_100km: no extent sourced; centre Wikipedia 'McMurdo Dry Valleys' coordinate (-77.46667, 162.51667)
regions.analog_quote: 'The best known Earth analog to the Martian high-northern plains' (NASA technical report, McMurdo Dry Valleys - a Mars Phoenix mission analog).

regions.name: Mauna Kea (Hawaii, USA)
regions.radius_rule: default_conservative_100km: no extent sourced; centre Wikipedia 'Mauna Kea' coordinate (19.82056, -155.46806)
regions.analog_quote: 'The Big Island of Hawaii has several sites that are excellent analogs for areas on the Moon and/or Mars' (NASA NAI annual report 2010; Mauna Kea deployments on its slopes).

regions.name: Pilbara (Western Australia)
regions.radius_rule: equal_area: area 507,896 km2 (Wikipedia 'Pilbara', text read 2026-11-14, including offshore islands); centre Wikipedia coordinate (21 S, 119 E)
regions.analog_quote: West et al. (2010), 'The geology of Australian Mars analogue sites', Planetary and Space Science 58(4): 'along with the Pilbara region, where the oldest convincing evidence of life guides exploration for early life on Mars.'

regions.name: Kilbourne Hole maar (New Mexico, USA)
regions.radius_rule: default_conservative_100km: no extent sourced in the pages read; centre Wikipedia 'Kilbourne Hole' coordinate (31.97194, -106.96472)
regions.analog_quote: NASA Goddard field team: Kilbourne Hole 'a perfect analog site for testing the kinds of instruments that future explorers might use to investigate volcanic areas on the Moon, Mars and other rocky planets or moons'.

regions.name: S P Crater (Arizona, USA), Apollo astronaut training site
regions.radius_rule: default_conservative_100km: no extent sourced; centre Wikipedia 'S P Crater' coordinate template (35.5822254 N, 111.6318207 W)
regions.analog_quote: 'American astronauts have used the crater to train for moonwalking' (Wikipedia, S P Crater article, citing National Geographic).

regions.name: Desert RATS field sites around Flagstaff (Arizona, USA)
regions.radius_rule: default_conservative_100km: the Desert RATS article gives no coordinate; the centre is the Wikipedia coordinate of Flagstaff, Arizona, the place the article names for its 'planned locations surrounding Flagstaff'
regions.analog_quote: NASA's Desert RATS 'began in 1997, reviving Apollo-style lunar exploration training'; the field season takes place 'in planned locations surrounding Flagstaff, Arizona'.

regions.name: Wadi Rum protected area (Jordan)
regions.radius_rule: equal_area: protected area 721 km2 (Wikipedia 'Wadi Rum' infobox, read 2026-11-14); centre Wikipedia coordinate 29 35 35 N, 35 25 12 E
regions.analog_quote: NASA Earth Observatory, 'Movie Mars on Earth' (28 Aug 2021): the colors and textures of Wadi Rum 'are a close match to those found on Mars'; filmmakers have used the valley as a 'stand-in for Mars'.
